body.statement: Fix \(\mathcal K\), \((\mathcal J_k)_{k\in\mathcal K}\), and \(c_0(k)\in\mathcal J_k\). For an observed law \(P\), construct \(p\), \(m\), \(q\), \(\pi\), \(\theta(P)\), and \(R_P\) solely from the observed distribution, and set \(\Gamma_P(x)=\operatorname{Cov}_P\{R_P(O)\mid X=x\}\) and \(H_P(x)=N^{\prime}\Gamma_P(x)N\). Suppose retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment envelope hold, \(\operatorname{rank}H_P(X)=r_0\) almost surely, and every positive eigenvalue of \(H_P(X)\) lies in \([\kappa,\kappa^{-1}]\). Then \(P\) admits a full-data extension \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\) if and only if \[q_{k,c}(X)=q_{k,c_0(k)}(X)\quad P_X\text{-almost surely for every }k\in\mathcal K\text{ and }c\in\mathcal J_k.\] At every regular interior \(P\) satisfying these observable equalities, \(N^{\prime}R_P\) has conditional mean zero and the induced observed-law tangent space obeys \[\mathcal T_P^{\perp}=\mathcal C_P.\] Hence every regular gradient of \(\tau_{\omega}(P)\) differs from one fixed pairwise gradient by exactly one element of \(\mathcal C_P\).
body.justification: This is the load-bearing local full-data-to-observed equivalence that turns score-family optimization into semiparametric efficiency.
body.gap: Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2) give the analogous observable conditional-moment characterizations for single-date and staggered DiD; they do not establish the DDD-only full-data extension or exhaust the coupled eligibility-gap tangent space with shared histories and target-share derivatives.
body.consumer: The theorem certifies whether the conditional loading can be called canonical and whether overidentifying restrictions support specification tests.
